Undergraduates in the 2024 cohort reported daily use of at least one note-taking application [@lopez2023].

Of the 312 respondents, 214 used a phone rather than a laptop during lectures. That preference held across all four faculties. Handwritten notes persisted in mathematics, where 61 of 78 students still wrote on paper [@nakamura2022]. The interview data explain why: students described formulas as faster to draw than to type.

Two limits follow. Recruitment ran through a single mailing list, so students who ignore university mail are absent from the sample. The survey asked about a typical week rather than a specific one, and recall over a week is weaker than a diary entry [@bell2021].
